trade.safety.p: Scammers actively target this community. Four habits stop nearly all of them:
trade.safety.r1p: Never type your seed phrase into any website or share it with anyone — no admin, no support, no exceptions. Whoever has it owns everything.
trade.safety.r2p: Team members never DM first. "Support", giveaways and urgent wallet fixes arriving in your DMs are impersonators — verify in the public Discord.
trade.safety.r3p: Every wallet popup spends or approves something. If any site asks you to "validate", "sync" or "migrate" your wallet — close it. We will never ask that.
trade.safety.r4p: Phishing sites clone real ones. Reach marketplaces by typing the address or via the official Discord links channel — never from a DM'd link.

trade.safety.foot: These tips live under Guides → Stay safe whenever you need them.

trade.mmbug.notice: Your MetaMask version ({v}) has a known bug that can wrongly block purchases with a fake "not enough IMX" error.
trade.mmbug.detail: It's a MetaMask extension regression (versions 13.33 and up), not your wallet or this site — your real balances always show live in the bar above. Workarounds until MetaMask ships a fix: use MetaMask version 13.32 or lower (official MetaMask GitHub releases only), or a compatible wallet like Rabby. Nothing is at risk — the bug only blocks confirmations, it can't move funds.
trade.err.mmBugHint: Heads-up: if MetaMask claimed you don't have enough IMX, that's a known bug in your MetaMask version (see the notice above the tabs) — your real balances are in the top bar.

hero.subtitle: A friendly guide to what HCC is, how Creatures and LAND came together, and the new Player Council that puts holders in the room where creative decisions get made.
s1.h2: So… what is the Creature Club?
s1.lead: The Highrise Creature Club is built from two collectible NFT concepts: 11,111 one-of-a-kind creature avatars and the Highrise LAND NFTs that were brought into the same club. Hold either one and you're a member, with perks woven right into Highrise.
s1.nft.p: Think of an NFT as a one-of-a-kind digital collectible that's genuinely yours — recorded on the blockchain, not just sitting inside an app. Your Creature is yours to keep, wear, sell, or gift, and no one can copy or take it.
s1.cc.p: It's 11,111 unique creature avatars, plus the Highrise LAND parcels folded into the same family. Members unlock wearable looks, daily Creature Coins, exclusive drops, and members-only spaces woven right into Highrise.
s1.cc.note: Gen 2 is on the way: every LAND will receive its own Creature, and every Gen 1 Creature its own pet — so Creatures and LAND end up equal in perks.
s1.join.h: How do I become a member?
s1.join.p: Just own a Creature or a LAND NFT — that's the whole requirement. Either one grants full Creature Club status: daily Creature Coins, exclusive drops, and the private community spaces.
s1.join.note: Your Discord role is automatic. Once your NFT sits in a wallet linked to your Highrise account, your roles update on their own — usually within an hour. Nothing to claim on your side.
s1.p1p: Every item on your creature is yours to wear inside Highrise.
s1.p2p: Earn coins daily to spin exclusive grabs only members can reach.
s1.p3p: Early and free access to fresh creature content as it ships.
s1.p4p: An exclusive club room and a real seat at the community table.
land.perks.summary: LAND owners earn Creature Coins (Premium plots at 3×), get room capacity boosts, keep their slime pets, and take part in the same drops and giveaways as Creature holders.
land.body: LAND NFTs are the club's collection of virtual parcels in the Highrise universe, in Standard and Premium tiers — and most LAND owners also have an adorable slime pet to go with their plot. LAND's original standalone plan changed, so the project was folded into the Creature Club family: owning LAND now makes you a member too.
land.p1p: Your pet stays yours — a collectible creature companion all its own.
land.p2p: Link a plot to a room to raise its capacity — 75 for Standard, 120 for Premium.
land.p3p: Premium LAND earns triple the Creature Coins of Standard, like Legendary creatures do.
land.p4p: LAND NFT owners now earn Creature Coins and join in club drops and giveaways.
journey.lead: No spin — just the honest arc of where the club has been and where it's headed.
t1.p: HCC launches as Highrise's first collectible avatar project: programmatically generated creatures, each with a wearable set of items and a promise of perks for holders.
t2.p: LAND launches as virtual parcels of the Highrise universe, in Standard and Premium tiers — with daily Land Tokens, room capacity boosts, an exclusive shop, and slime pets. The original dream: custom, monetizable corners of Highrise you could run yourself.
t3.p: Lots of ambition across both projects, but consistency, communication and follow-through didn't meet the standard holders deserved. We heard the frustration loud and clear.
t4.p: The original "custom monetizable Highrise" plan for LAND was wound down, and LAND owners were brought into Creature Club benefits. Land Tokens converted to Creature Coins, pets stayed with their owners, Premium LAND mirrored higher-tier Creature benefits at 3×, and a compensation path covered owners who did not want the new direction.
t5.h: LAND benefits become real HCC benefits
t5.p: Regular updates confirmed the practical merge: Discord access opened to LAND owners, Highrise+ eligibility and Creature Coins applied to eligible players, exclusive LAND and Creature giveaways continued, and Gen 2 / shop work moved forward under one HCC update rhythm.
t6.p: A dedicated artist put permanently on finishing Gen 1 & Gen 2. Bi-weekly updates. Monthly shop refreshes. Quarterly drops. A clear commitment to communication, delivery, and rebuilding trust one update at a time.
t7.p: The next step: a holder-led Player Council that helps shape what gets made — across Creatures and LAND alike. Head to the Council page to see how it works.
honest.p: Trust doesn't come back from promises — it comes from consistent delivery and from actually listening. The Council exists so HCC holders aren't just told what's coming next, but help decide it. It's a sounding board with real teeth on creative direction, run alongside the team that builds.
unify.h2: One club: Creatures + LAND, together
unify.lead: For a long time, Creatures and LAND lived as two separate NFT projects with two separate stories. The goal now is to unify them into a single Creature Club concept — one community, one set of benefits, one roadmap, and one holder voice.
unify.p1p: Land Tokens became Creature Coins, so everyone earns and spends the same way.
unify.p2p: Hold a Creature NFT or LAND NFT and you're a full member with the same core perks.
unify.p3p: Drops, Gen 2 and shop updates serve the whole club, not two parallel tracks.
unify.p4p: The Player Council represents Creature and LAND holders alike.
unify.note: Your assets don't change — your creature, your LAND plot, and your slime pet stay exactly as they are. Unifying is about the experience around them: one family that's easier to grow, support and build for.
council.member.note: Every HCC holder — Creature or LAND — is a member; hold for 3 months and you can vote. A Council "seat" is a formal elected role on top of that: only 7 exist, and you vote on who fills 4 of them.
council.lead: A small, holder-led group that works with a dedicated PM and the art team to finish Gen 2 and run the steady drops. It's advisory with teeth — a real say on creative, not a vote on the business.
council.legend.elected: Elected — chosen by a holder vote
council.legend.appointed: Appointed — 2 from Pocket Worlds + 1 trusted holder
council.fact2: one holder, one vote per seat — never whale-weighted
brackets.lead: Your bracket is set by how many HCC assets you hold (Creatures + LAND combined) when the candidacy window opens. Every holder size has a path to run.
brackets.why.p: So the Council can't be dominated by the largest holders. Every tier of the community has at least one seat reserved for someone who actually lives in it — a holder with a single Creature has a real shot, not just in theory.
brackets.run.p: Meet your bracket's asset count at the snapshot, have held at least 1 HCC asset continuously for 3 months (same bar as voters), and self-nominate during the open window by answering the application's open questions on your positions. Brackets gate running, not voting — every eligible holder votes on all 4 races.
vote.lead: You vote in every seat race, with one vote per seat — the Member race elects two, so you pick two candidates there. The candidates with the most votes win. One holder's vote is never weighted by how much you hold.
vote.p1p: Vote here on the site — sign in with Discord (linked to your Highrise account) so we can confirm you're an eligible holder.
vote.p2p: Individual votes are never published — only per-seat tallies. You get a private receipt to confirm your vote was counted.
vote.p3p: Votes are final once cast, and most election statistics are published right here on the site.
vote.p4p: If a race has no more candidates than seats, you vote to seat them or to reopen nominations. If reopening wins but nobody new steps up, the original candidate is seated — a seat can be contested, never blocked into a vacancy.
vaa.lead: To help you vote on substance rather than name recognition, the site includes a Voting Advice Application.
vaa.p1p: Candidates answer a set of open questions in their own words. The tool turns each answer into a clear position the candidate reviews and confirms.
vaa.p2p: You answer the same questions, then see a ranked affinity score for every candidate.
vaa.p3p: It never casts a vote for you — it's advice. The full methodology is published.
power.h2: Where the Council has real power
power.lead: Some calls the Council makes. Some it advises on. A few it's simply kept in the loop on — and that scope grows as it proves out.
power.row2: Which creatures & variants make a Gen 2 set
power.row3: The exclusive holder items in each drop
power.note: Pocket Worlds stays the executor and keeps final say on anything touching the economy, brand or legal guardrails — so the things that protect the whole club stay protected.
seat.p1p: Hold at least 1 HCC asset (Creature or LAND) continuously for 3 months to vote. To run: 2 seats are open to holders of 1–4 assets, 1 is reserved for holders of 5–14 assets, and 1 for holders of 15+ — so every holder size has a voice.
seat.p2p: A Council seat is tied to you — never bought or traded, same spirit as the club itself.
seat.p3p: A self-nomination window opens — you answer a few open questions on your positions — then holders vote. Clean and open.
seat.p4p: Six-month terms, max two in a row for elected seats. No entrenchment.
rhythm.p1: The PM owns the roadmap and brings the Council clear, scoped questions — each with a "done looks like this" attached. The Council weighs in on specific decisions, not endless open debate.
rhythm.p2: Cadence: a quick check-in every two weeks, plus a live call once a month. Where: a private holder channel to start, with token-gated holder-wide votes for the bigger questions down the line.
faq.q1: Is this a DAO? Do I own part of the company now?
faq.a1: No. The Council is advisory — a powerful sounding board on creative and roadmap decisions. Pocket Worlds remains the executor and keeps final say on the business, the economy and the brand.
faq.q2: Will big holders just take over?
faq.a2: No. It's one holder, one vote in every seat — never weighted by how many Creature or LAND assets you own. How many you hold only affects which seat you can run for — we reserve seats for different holder sizes so everyone is represented — never how much your vote counts. And 4 of the 7 seats are elected directly by holders, with 3 appointed for continuity and competence. We're stating that split openly rather than pretending it's purely democratic.
faq.a3: A dedicated artist is on finishing them, and the Council helps decide which creatures and variants make each Gen 2 set — picking from the options the art team can actually build.
faq.q4: I own LAND, not a Creature — am I in the club?
faq.a4: Yes. LAND owners are full Creature Club members. Your Land Tokens became Creature Coins, you earn daily Coins (Premium plots at 3×), and you take part in club drops and giveaways. Your plot and your slime pet stay exactly as they are.
faq.a5: Yes. Plans to migrate creatures off the blockchain have been cancelled following Steam approval. If that ever needs to change, we'll tell you early and clearly — no surprises.
faq.q6: What does the Council actually start with?
faq.a6: It starts advisory-leaning, and its "Decides" power grows release by release as it proves out. Think training wheels that come off over time, not everything on day one.
faq.q7: How much does a Creature cost — and what if I can't afford one yet?
faq.a7: Prices are set by holders, so they range widely — from a few hundred dollars to several thousand, depending on rarity and traits. For live numbers, the Market page shows the current floor and real sale history. Can't buy in yet? Keep an eye on the Highrise Discord — there are regular giveaways and contests where you can win one for free.
faq.q8: I bought a Creature but don't see my role or perks yet — what gives?
faq.a8: First, make sure the wallet holding it is linked to your Highrise account — that's what connects your NFTs to the club. Once it's linked, your Discord roles and perks sync on their own, usually within an hour. If it's been longer, double-check you linked the right wallet, then ask in the public Highrise Discord.
faq.q9: Which marketplace do I use — and how do I avoid fakes?
faq.a9: Gen 1 Creatures trade on Token Trove (Immutable zkEVM). LAND and Gen 2 live on OpenSea, under the "Highrise LAND" collection. Important: Gen 1 Creatures are not on OpenSea — any "Highrise Creature" or "Highrise Creature Club" collection you see there is a fake scam. Always reach a marketplace through the official links in the Highrise Discord, never a random DM.
roadmap.lead: From the next drop to Gen 2 — every milestone we're working toward, in order.
rm.m1.p: The 4th anniversary recolour grab is dropping next — pink and white recolours, exclusive to HCC members.
rm.medu.p: Clear, accessible content explaining what HCC NFTs are, how they work, and what holding one actually means — lowering the barrier for new and existing members alike.
rm.m2.p: Finalising the council rules: candidacy eligibility, the appointed seat process, and anti-gaming guardrails. The structure needs to be right before the clock starts.
rm.m3.p: Application window, campaign period, and voting date — all locked in and published here. No more guessing when.
rm.m4.p: Self-nominations open, community votes. 4 seats filled by holders, 3 appointed for continuity. One holder, one vote.
rm.m7.p: The council weighs in on its first real creative questions: next drop theme, Gen 2 variants, Creature Shop priorities.
rm.m9.p: The council reviews Gen 2 designs before they're final. Structured feedback from holders, not a leaked WIP.
rm.m10.p: Gen 2 Creatures released as a proper event — not a quiet drop. Marketing, a community launch moment, and a clear Gen 1 vs Gen 2 utility story.
rm.note: Milestones in approximate order — dates announced as confirmed
g2.lead: Six full creature sets are being built right now — the biggest content push in club history. Follow the road, stop by stop, to see exactly where each set stands.
g2.sets.lead: Follow the line — one stop per set, in production order. Each stop shows the four phases a set walks before it lands in Highrise.
g2.pipe.lead: Every set walks the same four steps. So when an update says "final art", you'll know exactly where that set stands.
g2.pipe.s1.p: The set's look and attitude get locked.
g2.pipe.s2.p: Artists explore options across all 17 trait categories.
g2.pipe.s3.p: The chosen designs are drawn for every item in the set.
g2.pipe.s4.p: Every item is cleaned and finished — front and back.
g2.word.c1p: A work-in-progress update every two weeks — even when it's not pretty or finished. Silence is the one thing you'll never get.
g2.word.c3p: If a date has to move, you'll hear it from us early — with the why. We won't rush a set out broken.
g2.note: Set order and pacing can shift as the Council weighs in — every change gets explained in the bi-weekly updates
perks.h2: What are the perks of owning a Creature?
perks.lead: These are some of the perks and benefits of owning a Highrise Creature or LAND.
perks.p1p: Wear each item in your Creature outfit inside the Highrise Metaverse.
perks.p2p: Access to the exclusive Creature Club Room in Highrise and the Creature-Club Discord channel.
perks.p3p: Daily Creature Coins based on your eligible NFTs; Premium LAND grants 75 Creature Coins instead of 25.
perks.p4p: Highrise+ Tier 1 each month when eligibility is met: keep a Creature or LAND NFT linked for at least 30 uninterrupted days before renewal and log in for seven consecutive days leading up to the new month. Subscriptions renew only on the first day of each month.
perks.p5p: Exclusive Creature-themed content airdropped to your inventory's gift section at surprise intervals.
coins.lead: Creature Coins are special tokens awarded daily to all owners of a Creature or LAND, to spin exclusive grabs within the Highrise app.
coins.req: To receive these coins, you must own at least one Highrise Creature Club NFT and have your wallet connected to the Highrise website.
coins.epic.p: Each Epic Creature owned awards 25 Creature Coins daily.
coins.legendary.p: Each Legendary Creature owned awards 75 Creature Coins daily.

footer.h2: Built with the club, for the club.
footer.p: This is the start of HCC holders having a real hand in what gets made. More to come — every two weeks, like we promised.
terms.accept: Acceptance. Voters tick "I agree to the Terms" after logging in with Discord, before their first ballot; candidates explicitly accept at nomination submission. Acceptance is recorded with your Highrise Person ID, Discord ID, and a timestamp.
terms.s1.p: The Council is advisory only; Pocket Worlds keeps final say on business, economy, brand and legal. A seat is not ownership, equity, a security, a token right, employment, or any financial entitlement, and is not a DAO membership.
terms.s2.p: Participation is voluntary and unpaid. There is no employment, contractor, or partnership relationship. Any perks are discretionary, revocable gifts — never payment or a right.
terms.s3.p:
Holdings = combined Creatures + LAND at the published snapshot.
  • Voters: held at least 1 HCC NFT continuously for the 3 months ending at the snapshot.
  • Candidates: meet the bracket asset count at the candidacy snapshot and the 3-month continuous-holding bar; self-nominate in the window by answering the application's open questions.
  • Eligibility is assessed against your Highrise account's current primary wallet (holdings across multiple wallets are not aggregated). Snapshots are final.
terms.s4.p: One vote per elected seat (4 seats, plurality). You authenticate by logging in with Discord, which we match to your Highrise account to confirm eligibility — no wallet connection or signing is required, and we never move or spend your assets. Voting is per Highrise account (one person, one vote per seat). Votes are final once cast and cannot be changed. Vote privacy: individual votes are not published — only per-seat tallies are. Each voter gets a private, verifiable receipt to confirm their vote was recorded and counted; the receipt is yours alone and does not reveal your choice to others.
terms.s5.p: By self-nominating you grant Pocket Worlds a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to publish, display, translate, and process your answers to the application's open questions for the election and the Voting Advice Application (VAA). The tool maps each written answer to a position, but your confirmed positions are authoritative — you review and edit them before voting opens, and your confirmed positions are published. You are responsible for the accuracy of your submission. The full VAA methodology will be published. All candidacies are subject to review of account background and any community reports; Pocket Worlds may decline or remove a candidacy at its discretion, and the reasons will be disclosed privately to the affected candidate.
terms.s6.p: Elected terms run 6 months, max two consecutive for elected seats. Seats are personal and non-transferable — never sold, lent, or assigned. You may resign at any time. A seat left vacant mid-term stays empty until the next election — vacancies are not backfilled during a term.
terms.s7.p: The Council operates openly: members are under no confidentiality obligation and may discuss and share Council materials publicly. Accordingly, Pocket Worlds will share with the Council only materials it is comfortable being made public — nothing shared should be assumed secret or treated as a leak.
terms.s8.p: No harassment, hate, threats, or doxxing. No vote-buying, bribery, or exchanging anything of value for votes. No impersonation, fraud, or material misrepresentation. No sybil/multi-account voting and no snapshot manipulation. Disclose conflicts of interest. Follow Highrise/HCC community guidelines and applicable law.
terms.s9.p: One eligible account, one ballot per seat. Pocket Worlds may void votes, disqualify candidates, remove members, or bar future participation for breach — at its reasonable discretion, with reasons published where practical.
terms.s10.p: To authenticate and check eligibility we process your Discord ID, Highrise ID, Person ID, linked wallet address(es) and wallet-change history (via Discord OAuth and Highrise's internal API), plus the holdings snapshot, vote records (kept private), candidate answers (public), and voter answers (private; used to compute your own affinity, not published per-user). Candidate answers are sent to Anthropic (Claude) so the tool can map each into a position the candidate confirms. On-chain/wallet data is inherently public. See the Privacy Policy for retention and deletion-request handling.
terms.s11.p: Provided "as is." The VAA affinity score is advisory and not guaranteed accurate. Nothing here is financial, investment, tax, or legal advice, a securities offering, or a guarantee of any NFT's value. Liability is limited to the extent permitted by law; candidates indemnify Pocket Worlds for content they submit.
privacy.who.p: The HCC Player Council election is operated by Pocket Worlds ("we", "us"). This policy explains what we collect, why, who we share it with, and your choices. Data requests/questions: Highrise Discord support channel.
privacy.collect.p:
• Account & identity: via Discord OAuth — your Discord ID and the basic profile you authorize; via Highrise's internal API — your Highrise ID, Person ID, linked wallet address(es), and wallet-change history.
  • Eligibility: HCC NFT holdings and transfer history for your current primary wallet, read from public blockchains.
  • Participation: candidate answers and positions (public), voter answers (private), votes (private), and terms-acceptance records.
  • Technical: a login session cookie and basic server logs (e.g., IP, timestamps) for security.
privacy.use.p: To authenticate you; verify eligibility (3-month holding + bracket); run the VAA matching; record and tally votes and issue your private receipt; publish candidate answers/positions and aggregate results; review candidacies and enforce election integrity.
privacy.cookies.p: A single session cookie keeps you logged in after Discord OAuth. No third-party advertising or tracking cookies.
privacy.share.p:
• Anthropic (Claude) — candidate answers are sent to Anthropic to map each written answer to a position the candidate then reviews and confirms. Voter data and individual votes are not sent to Anthropic.
  • Discord — for OAuth login.
  • Highrise / Pocket Worlds internal systems — identity and eligibility resolution.
  • Public blockchain explorers (Immutable/Blockscout, etc.) — we query public chain data.
  • Hosting/infrastructure — to run the site and store election data.
We do not sell your personal data.
privacy.public.p: Public: candidate answers, candidate positions, and aggregate election statistics — most election statistics (per-seat tallies, turnout, bracket breakdowns, etc.) are published on the website. Private: your individual vote (never published), your voter answers, and your vote receipt. Wallet/on-chain data is inherently public on the blockchain.
privacy.retention.p: We retain election data for an undetermined period — there is no fixed deletion schedule. You may still request deletion of your personal data as described below.
privacy.rights.p: You may request access to or deletion of your personal data — subject to legal and election-integrity limits — by contacting Highrise Discord support channel. Where applicable law (e.g., GDPR/CCPA) grants further rights, we honor them.
privacy.security.p: We use reasonable technical and organizational measures; no system is perfectly secure. The election algorithms and the website's structure are open-source and auditable by all users, so anyone can inspect how data is processed and how votes are counted.
privacy.children.p: The election is not directed to children, consistent with Highrise's policies.
privacy.changes.p: We may update this policy; all changes are published on the website and in Discord. Contact: Highrise Discord support channel.

contrib.gate.h: This site is yours to shape
contrib.gate.p: Every line of this site is public on GitHub — the pages, the styles, even the election logic. Spot a typo, have an idea, or want to ship a fix? You're welcome to. No NFT required.
contrib.why.lead: The Council gives holders a voice in what gets made. Keeping this site open is the same idea, in code — a place where anyone can check the work and help make it better.
contrib.why.c1p: The election logic and the whole site are open to read. You don't have to take our word for how votes are counted — you can check it yourself.
contrib.why.c2h: A real say, in code too
contrib.why.c2p: Beyond voting, this is another way to leave your mark on the club — propose a change, and it can become part of the live site.
contrib.why.c3p: A fixed typo, a clearer guide, a smoother mobile layout — small improvements add up for everyone who visits.
contrib.why.c4p: This site is built with the community, for the community. Your fixes and ideas are how that promise stays real.
contrib.ways.lead: You don't have to write code to help. Every one of these makes the site better — pick whatever fits you.
contrib.ways.c1p: Something broken, misaligned, or showing the wrong info? Open an issue and tell us what you saw.
contrib.ways.c2p: A new section, a clearer flow, a feature you'd love — float it as an issue and let's talk it through.
contrib.ways.c3p: Catch a typo or confusing wording? Even a one-word fix is a welcome pull request.
contrib.ways.c4p: The site speaks 7 languages from files in locales/. Improve a translation, or help fill the gaps that fall back to English.
contrib.ways.c5p: Comfortable with HTML, CSS, or vanilla JS? Fork the repo and open a pull request with your change.
contrib.ways.c6p: Found something sensitive? Report it privately to the team in the Highrise Discord rather than opening a public issue.
contrib.how.lead: Four steps from idea to pull request. There's no build step and no framework — just plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JS.
contrib.how.s1p: On GitHub, hit Fork to get your own copy of the project, then clone it to your machine.
contrib.how.s2p: Start the small Node server and open the site in your browser to see your changes live as you work.
contrib.how.s3h: Make your change on a branch
contrib.how.s3p: Create a branch named for what you're doing — like fix/mobile-layout or feat/faq-entry — then make and test your edit. New copy goes through the i18n keys in locales/en.json.
contrib.how.s4p: Push your branch and open a pull request against main. We'll review it with you right there in the PR.
contrib.how.note: Keep each pull request focused on one thing — a single fix or a single feature. It makes review faster and the history cleaner.
contrib.merged.lead: Nothing goes live without review. Here's the kind of change that sails through.
contrib.merged.i1: Bug fixes that are accurate and tested
contrib.merged.i2: Content that's factually correct about HCC
contrib.merged.i3: Visual and UX improvements that match the existing style
contrib.merged.note: Changes to the Council rules, the election process, or Pocket Worlds commitments need a sign-off from the team — no worries, just open the pull request and we'll discuss it there.
contrib.cta.p: Star the repo, open an issue, or ship your first fix. And if you get stuck, the community and team are a message away in the Highrise Discord.
guide.lead: Everything you need to buy, sell, move, and protect your HCC NFTs — step by step. Put together with the community.
guide.what.lead: Your creature and your LAND are NFTs — items you truly own on the blockchain, not just inside an app. Here's what that means.
guide.what.c1p: An NFT is a one-of-a-kind item recorded on the blockchain. Your creature is yours to keep, wear, sell, or gift.
guide.what.c2p: HCC creatures live on the Immutable zkEVM network — a fast, low-fee blockchain built for game items.
guide.what.c3p: Your wallet, like MetaMask, is how you prove ownership and move your assets. Guard it like your house keys.
guide.what.c4p: Token Trove is the marketplace where you buy, sell, and transfer your creatures.
guide.kit.lead: Four things you'll meet again and again. Get familiar and the rest is easy.
guide.kit.c1p: Your crypto wallet. Holds your funds and creatures, and signs every action. Get it as a browser extension or mobile app.
guide.kit.c2p: The official HCC marketplace. Find the link in the Highrise Discord under official links — never from a random DM.
guide.kit.c3p: Ethereum ($ETH) is the currency you use to buy creatures.
guide.kit.c4p: Immutable X ($IMX) covers the tiny network fee ("gas") on every action. Keep a little on hand.
guide.kit.network: Creatures live on the Immutable zkEVM network. You'll switch your wallet to it when buying or moving creatures — Token Trove walks you through it each time.
guide.steps.lead: Six short guides, in the order you'll likely need them. Pick a step below — most come with a community video to follow along.
guide.g1.h: Find Token Trove & link your wallet
guide.g1.p: Get to the official marketplace and connect MetaMask so you can see your balances and creatures.
guide.g1.s1: Open the Highrise Discord and go to the official links channel. Find the link to buy Highrise creatures — it takes you straight to Token Trove.
guide.g1.s2: Have your MetaMask wallet ready — extension or mobile app — and make sure you're logged in.
guide.g1.s3: On Token Trove, click Connect Wallet. Choose Immutable zkEVM, then pick MetaMask.
guide.g1.s4: Approve the connection in MetaMask. Token Trove now shows your balances — ETH, IMX, USDC — and your creatures under My NFTs.
guide.g2.p: Bridging moves your crypto from Ethereum mainnet to the Immutable zkEVM network where creatures live. Before bridging, you'll need a small amount of $IMX — every action on Immutable requires it as a network fee. Balances can take 20–40 minutes to appear.
guide.g2.s1: Before anything else, swap a little $ETH to $IMX in MetaMask — $IMX is the fee currency for every action on Immutable zkEVM (buying, selling, transferring). Around 0.0025 $ETH worth is plenty to start. Do this swap before bridging.
guide.g2.s2: On Token Trove, confirm you're connected and logged in, and that you can see the Bridge button. Click Bridge.
guide.g2.s3: Bridge $IMX first. Pick $IMX as the token, enter an amount (e.g. 20 $IMX), check the small fee, and confirm.
guide.g2.s4: Your wallet switches to Ethereum mainnet automatically. Confirm the two MetaMask pop-ups — the network fee, then the transfer itself.
guide.g2.s5: Now bridge your ETH the same way — this is what you'll buy creatures with. Pick ETH, enter an amount (e.g. 0.025), and confirm the single request.
guide.g2.s6: Wait roughly 20–40 minutes. When it's done, your $ETH and $IMX balances appear on Token Trove, ready to use.
guide.g2.note: Remember: $ETH buys creatures, $IMX pays the gas. You need a little $IMX for anything you do on Immutable — buying, selling, or transferring.
guide.g3.p: With funds bridged over, you're ready to shop the collection or list one of your own.
guide.g3.s1: Browse the collection and pick the creature you want. Before buying, switch your wallet to the Immutable zkEVM network: open MetaMask, select Immutable zkEVM, then refresh the page.
guide.g3.s2: Click Buy Now. Review the small network fee (this is what IMX is for) and click Confirm.
guide.g3.s3: Once the blockchain confirms, the creature is yours. Refresh your balances and check My NFTs to see it.
guide.g3.s4: To sell, open one of your creatures and click List Now. Set your price and confirm the signature request in MetaMask.
guide.g3.s5: Your creature is now listed. Anyone can buy it directly — you don't have to do anything else until it sells.
guide.g3.note: When a creature sells, a 5% creator royalty is built into the smart contract and comes out of the sale price automatically — worth factoring into the price you set.
guide.g4.h: Transfer a creature to another wallet
guide.g4.p: Send a creature straight to another wallet — handy for moving between your own wallets or gifting.
guide.g4.s1: Open the creature you want to send and click the Transfer button — the little paper-airplane icon.
guide.g4.s2: Paste the destination wallet address. Double-check it — transfers can't be undone.
guide.g4.s3: Review the small gas fee and click Confirm. The Immutable zkEVM network confirms the transfer.
guide.g4.s4: After a few seconds, refresh My NFTs. The creature leaves your wallet and lands in the new one. A full page refresh helps if it lingers.
guide.g4.note: Always paste and verify the address yourself. There's no undo, and no one can reverse a transfer to the wrong wallet.
guide.g5.p: Connect your wallet to your Highrise account so your creatures, items, and perks show up in the app.
guide.g5.s1: Open the Highrise Discord, go to official links, and click the top one — the Highrise website. Log into your account.
guide.g5.s2: Go to your account Settings and scroll to the bottom, to Connect MetaMask Wallet. Make sure you're logged into the MetaMask wallet you want to link.
guide.g5.s3: Click Connect MetaMask Wallet. When highrise.game asks to connect, click Connect.
guide.g5.s4: Confirm the signature request — it just lets Highrise read your wallet. You're linked, and your creatures now show up in Highrise under Your Collections.
guide.g6.h: Mint LAND you bought with Deeds
guide.g6.p: Bought a parcel during an in-app LAND Deeds sale? It lives inside Highrise until you mint it onto the blockchain. Minting is what lets you sell, transfer, or trade it on OpenSea.
guide.g6.cap: Withdrawing a plot from your Highrise inventory
guide.g6.s1: Go to highrise.game and log in with the Highrise account that holds your plot. Make sure your MetaMask wallet is ready.
guide.g6.s2: Click your avatar in the top-right corner, then open Inventory. Your plot (or plots) shows up there.
guide.g6.s3: Click the specific plot you want to put on-chain, then press Withdraw.
guide.g6.s4: MetaMask pops up — Confirm and Sign the transaction. Keep a little ETH in your wallet to cover the gas fee.
guide.g6.s5: Once it confirms, your parcel is minted onto the blockchain and ready to trade, sell, or transfer on OpenSea.
guide.g6.note: Until you mint it, the plot stays tied to the Highrise account it was bought with — it can't move between accounts or wallets until it's on-chain.
gm.h2: Trade right here, step by step
gm.lead: A full walkthrough of the in-site marketplace — non-custodial, 0% marketplace fee, and every action signed by your own wallet. Flip each step between Creatures and LAND. It's in Beta, so trades are real — start small.
gm.setup.p: Open the Trade tab and connect your wallet. A quick safety check appears first, then your balances show in the bar up top.
gm.setup.cr.s1: Open the Trade tab and keep the collection on Creatures. Tap Connect MetaMask — read and accept the quick safety reminder first.
gm.setup.cr.s2: Approve the connection in MetaMask. If you're on the wrong network, tap Switch network — the site adds Immutable zkEVM for you.
gm.setup.cr.s3: Once connected, the top bar shows your wallet, your ETH and IMX balances, and "Your Creatures".
gm.setup.cr.note: Only self-custody wallets like MetaMask can trade here. If your Creatures are in Immutable Passport, withdraw them to MetaMask first.
gm.setup.la.s1: Open the Trade tab and switch the collection to LAND. Tap Connect MetaMask and accept the safety reminder.
gm.setup.la.s2: When prompted, switch MetaMask to Ethereum mainnet — that's where LAND parcels live.
gm.setup.la.s3: Connected, the top bar shows your wallet, your mainnet ETH, and "Your LAND".
gm.setup.la.note: LAND trades settle on Ethereum mainnet — there's no network to add, just switch MetaMask to Ethereum.
gm.fund.h: Get funds on the right network
gm.fund.p: Make sure the coins you'll spend sit on the same network as the asset — the panel guides you if you're short.
gm.fund.cr.where: Creatures need ETH for the price and a little IMX for gas — both on Immutable zkEVM.
gm.fund.cr.s1: Tap Buy on any Creature. If your ETH is on Ethereum mainnet, the panel offers to bridge it to Immutable zkEVM (powered by Squid) — confirm the two MetaMask pop-ups.
gm.fund.cr.s2: No IMX for gas yet? The same panel swaps a tiny bit of ETH into IMX on Immutable zkEVM — a little lasts a long time.
gm.fund.cr.s3: Bridges take a few minutes; a progress bar tracks it. When your ETH and IMX land, come back and tap Buy.
gm.fund.cr.note: ETH pays the price, IMX pays the gas — and both must be on Immutable zkEVM, not Ethereum mainnet.
gm.fund.la.where: LAND is bought with plain ETH on Ethereum mainnet — no bridging, no IMX.
gm.fund.la.s1: Hold enough ETH on Ethereum mainnet to cover the parcel's price plus mainnet gas.
gm.fund.la.s2: Short on mainnet ETH? Top up your wallet first — MetaMask's Buy feature or a withdrawal from an exchange both work.
gm.fund.la.note: LAND uses mainnet ETH for both the price and gas — there's nothing to bridge and no IMX needed.
gm.trade.p: The heart of the marketplace — find what you want, buy it, or list your own. We charge 0% marketplace fee.
gm.trade.cr.where: Creatures: Immutable zkEVM, with offers and instant-sell.
gm.trade.cr.s1: Browse "On sale now". Filter by rarity, traits and price, search by name or number, and sort by price, rarity or newest. Flip to "All Creatures" for the whole collection.
gm.trade.cr.s2: Buy: open a Creature, check the all-in price (price + royalty + gas, 0% fee), tap Buy now — approve ETH once, then confirm.
gm.trade.cr.s3: Offer: place an offer in ETH on any Creature, or a collection-wide "offer to buy any". Sign once (free, no gas); if a holder accepts, it arrives automatically.
gm.trade.cr.s4: Sell: Sell tab → pick a Creature → set a price in ETH or your currency → approve the collection once, then sign (free). Manage under "Your listings", or instantly sell into the top offer.
gm.trade.cr.note: 0% marketplace fee. Buyers pay the 5% creator royalty, and listings and offers are free to create — just a signature.
gm.trade.la.where: LAND: Ethereum mainnet via OpenSea. No offers yet.
gm.trade.la.s1: Browse parcels by their Slime pet — filter and rank by the Slime's traits and rarity, since the plots look alike. On-sale parcels show all-in ETH prices from OpenSea.
gm.trade.la.s2: Buy: open a listed parcel, review the all-in ETH price (0% fee from us), tap Buy now and confirm in MetaMask. Ethereum mainnet gas applies.
gm.trade.la.s3: Sell: Sell tab → pick a parcel → set price and a listing length → approve OpenSea once, then sign (free). It lists on OpenSea and shows here.
gm.trade.la.note: A LAND sale costs 1% OpenSea + 5% creator royalty. Offers aren't available for LAND yet.
gm.move.p: Send an asset straight to another wallet — your own or a friend's. Transfers can't be undone, so we help you check the address.
gm.move.cr.s1: Open the Transfer tab and pick the Creature to send. Listed Creatures are hidden — cancel the listing first.
gm.move.cr.s2: Paste the recipient's Immutable zkEVM address. We run live safety checks — checksum, contract detection, brand-new-wallet warnings — and flag anything risky.
gm.move.cr.s3: Review, tap Send Creature, then confirm in MetaMask. Follow it on the explorer link.
gm.move.cr.note: Transfers are permanent — a little IMX covers gas, and no one can reverse a send to the wrong wallet, so double-check the address.
gm.move.la.s1: Open the Transfer tab with LAND selected and pick the parcel to send.
gm.move.la.s2: Paste the recipient's Ethereum address and re-read it carefully — transfers can't be undone.
gm.move.la.s3: Confirm in MetaMask. Mainnet gas applies; track the transaction on Etherscan.
gm.move.la.note: LAND transfers settle on Ethereum mainnet and pay mainnet gas.
gm.game.p: Owning the NFT is half the fun — link your wallet to Highrise so it shows up and unlocks its perks in the app.
gm.game.cr.where: Creatures appear in your Highrise clothing inventory.
gm.game.cr.s1: On highrise.game, open Settings → Connect MetaMask Wallet and link the wallet holding your Creature.
gm.game.cr.s2: Sign the request. Within an hour your Creature outfit appears on the second tab of your Highrise clothing inventory, and your Discord roles update.
gm.game.cr.s3: Wear the items, earn daily Creature Coins, and join the members-only spaces.
gm.game.cr.note: Linking is read-only — it just lets Highrise see your wallet. Your keys never leave MetaMask.
gm.game.la.where: LAND brings its Slime pet and perks into Highrise.
gm.game.la.s1: Link the wallet holding your parcel to your Highrise account in Settings, the same way.
gm.game.la.s2: Your parcel and its Slime pet show up in your account, with room-capacity boosts and daily Creature Coins (Premium plots at 3×).
gm.game.la.s3: Check the Slime Pet Map under Guides → Links to see which Slime belongs to your plot.
gm.game.la.note: LAND owners are full Creature Club members — the same drops, giveaways and Coins as Creature holders.
guide.safe.lead: Your creatures are valuable and ownership is final. A few habits keep them safe.
guide.safe.c1p: Your seed phrase is the 12 random words shown once when you created your wallet — it's the master key. Whoever has it controls your wallet completely. No one — not Highrise, not support — will ever need it.
guide.safe.c2p: Only use links from the Highrise Discord's official links channel. Never trust marketplace or wallet links sent via DMs, social media comments, or sites you didn't find yourself.
guide.safe.c3p: Before any transfer, paste and re-read the destination address. Transfers are permanent and can't be reversed.
guide.safe.c4p: Every action on Immutable needs a tiny $IMX fee. Keep a small balance so you're never stuck mid-transaction.
guide.safe.c6p: Every wallet popup spends or approves something. Slow down and read what it does. Sites asking you to "validate", "sync" or "migrate" your wallet are scams — no real app needs that.
guide.safe.c7p: Your Creatures live on the Immutable zkEVM network. Only transfer them to wallets on that same network, and don't use a marketplace's "withdraw" option to move a Creature off it unless you're certain what it does — sending to the wrong network means permanent, unrecoverable loss.
guide.safe.c8p: Gen 1 Creatures only trade on Token Trove. Any "Highrise Creature" or "Highrise Creature Club" collection on OpenSea is a fake — Gen 1 isn't listed there. Only LAND and Gen 2 are on OpenSea. Reach every marketplace through the official Discord links.
guide.safe.hacked.p: Clicked a bad link or signed something suspicious? Act fast: move your Creatures and funds to a fresh wallet first, then revoke old approvals from the compromised one, and tell the team in the public Discord so others get warned. Speed matters more than embarrassment — everyone has a close call eventually.
guide.safe.c5p: Real staff won't DM you first asking for wallet access, payments, or your phrase. When in doubt, ask in the public Discord.
guide.safe.alert: HCC staff and support will never message you first. If anyone DMs you claiming to be from the team — asking for wallet access, your seed phrase, or any payment — it's a scam. Ask publicly in the Highrise Discord instead.
guide.cta.p: Hop into the Highrise Discord and ask — the community and team are happy to help you get set up.

hub.apply.d: Sign in with Discord to check your eligibility to run or vote.
apply.lead: Sign in with the Discord account linked to your Highrise profile. We check your linked wallet against current HCC holders to confirm whether you can vote and which seat you can run for.
apply.fineprint: We only read your Discord identity and your linked wallet's public holdings. The 3-month continuous-holding rule for voting is verified against the official snapshot when the candidacy window opens.
apply.signin.intro: Your Discord account must be linked to your Highrise profile so we can find your wallet.
apply.trust.readonly: Read-only — we never touch your funds
apply.is.run: Eligible to run for a seat
apply.note.holdtime: Voting also requires holding at least 1 HCC asset continuously for 3 months. That's confirmed against the official snapshot when voting opens.
apply.note.nothold: We didn't find any HCC assets in your linked wallet, so you're not eligible to vote or run yet. Hold a Creature or LAND NFT to take part.
apply.note.vote: You're eligible to vote. To cast your ballot, just finish the quick candidate match below — your official ballot unlocks the moment you've reviewed your matches. You don't need to run for a seat or fill out the candidate application.
apply.nowallet.p: Your Discord account has no Highrise wallet linked, so we can't check your holdings. Link your wallet in your Highrise account settings, then sign in again.
apply.holders.loading: We're loading the current holder snapshot. Give it a moment and try again.
apply.err.denied: Sign-in was cancelled. You can try again whenever you're ready.
apply.err.state: Your sign-in session expired or didn't match. Please try signing in again.
apply.err.failed: Something went wrong during sign-in. Please try again.
apply.race.reopenuntil: Nominations reopened for this seat until {date}
apply.race.runoffuntil: Runoff for one seat — voting closes {date}
apply.race.foot: {elected} seats are filled by holder vote, plus {appointed} appointed for continuity.
apply.race.snapshot: Eligible voters were frozen in the official snapshot of {n} holder wallets taken {date}.
apply.race.foot.closed: These are the seats up for election — self-nominations open when the candidacy window starts.
apply.race.empty: No candidacies in yet — be the first to run.
apply.race.err: We couldn't load the election status. Try again in a moment.
apply.result.seatedByRule: nominations reopened and nobody new ran, so the seat is filled by rule
apply.result.reopened: Reopen nominations won — the candidacy window for this seat is open again
apply.result.reopenPending: Reopen nominations won — a new candidacy window will be announced
apply.result.revote: New candidates joined — this seat is decided by a fresh vote
apply.result.runoffcarried: {names} kept their seat from the first round
apply.result.vacant: No candidates ran — this seat is filled from the appointed track
apply.result.receipts.p: Every ballot cast in this race is listed here by its receipt code — codes are random and tied to neither voter nor choice. Find yours to confirm your vote was counted; the number of codes always equals the votes cast.
vote.intro: Set where you stand on each statement and we'll rank the candidates by how closely they align with you. Your answers are saved on this device and used only to work out your match — never stored, logged, or linked to you.
vote.private: Private — used only to compute your match, never stored or logged
vote.see.unlock: See my matches & unlock my ballot
vote.unlocknote: Voting's open. This is how you vote: finish this quick match and your official ballot unlocks right below — it's there to make sure every vote is an informed one.
vote.cleared: Cleared — your answers are gone from this device.
vote.answerfirst: Answer at least one statement to see your matches.
vote.toomany: Too many match requests — give it a minute and try again.
vote.namesHidden: You're seeing an anonymous preview for the candidacy phase. Candidate names and their full written answers stay hidden until voting opens — then every candidate's full profile becomes public.
vote.profile.locked: Their written answers stay hidden during the candidacy phase and become public when voting opens. For now you can compare where they stand above.
vote.profile.err: We couldn't load this candidate. Try again in a moment.
vote.empty: No candidates have submitted yet — check back once the field is set.
vote.err: We couldn't load the matcher. Try again in a moment.
vote.gate.signin.h: Sign in to find your match
vote.gate.signin.p: Sign in with Discord above to privately match yourself against the candidates. Your answers are used only to compute your match and are never stored or linked to you.
vote.gate.noteligible.p: We couldn't confirm any HCC holdings on your linked wallet, so candidate matching isn't available. Hold a Creature or LAND NFT to take part.
ballot.intro: You get one vote for each seat in a race — the Member race elects two, so you can pick two candidates there. Every eligible holder votes in all races. Each vote is final once cast, and you'll get a private receipt for it.
ballot.private: Secret ballot — only per-seat tallies are ever published
ballot.pick: Pick your candidate, then cast your vote.
ballot.multi.intro: This race elects {seats} seats, so you get {seats} votes. Pick your candidates one at a time — each is final once cast.
ballot.addmore: You have {n} more vote — pick another candidate for the remaining seat.
ballot.allcast: All your votes are in for this race
ballot.unopposed: This seat is unopposed. Seat {name}, or vote to reopen nominations — if reopening wins but nobody new runs, the seat goes to them anyway, so reopening only matters if someone steps up to compete.
ballot.unopposed.many: This race has no more candidates than seats. Seat {names}, or vote to reopen nominations — if reopening wins but nobody new runs, the seats go to them anyway.
ballot.opt.reopen.p: Ask for more candidates — the candidacy window reopens for this seat
ballot.confirm: Tap again to confirm — it's final
ballot.receipt.keep: Keep this code — it's your private proof that your vote was counted.
ballot.thanks: Voting has closed and your ballot was counted. Results are on the board above — these receipts are your proof.
ballot.verifynote: Each race's results on the board publish the full list of receipt codes — find yours there to verify your vote was counted.
ballot.concluded: This race has concluded — see the results board.
ballot.noCands: Nobody ran for this seat — it's filled from the appointed track.
ballot.already: You already voted in this race — votes are final.
ballot.err: We couldn't cast your vote. Try again in a moment.
ballot.loaderr: We couldn't load your ballot. Try again in a moment.
ballot.locked.p: Before your official ballot opens, use the voting advice above — set where you stand and see how each candidate lines up with you. Your ballot unlocks the moment you've reviewed your matches, so the names you pick are ones you actually know.
ballot.gate.snapshot.h: Your wallet isn't in the voting snapshot
ballot.gate.snapshot.p: To vote in this election, your wallet must already have been holding when the official snapshot was taken on {date} — and still be holding now. Assets picked up after the snapshot can't vote this time, but they'll count for the next election.
app.closed.banner: Applications open when the candidacy window starts. You can fill this in and save a draft now — submitting and AI drafting unlock when it opens.
app.intro: Tell holders where you stand. Your answers become your public candidate profile, so be clear and be yourself.
app.bracket.label: Running in
app.field.name.label: Ballot name
app.field.name.hint: This is your Highrise username — it's how you'll appear to voters.
app.field.name.notinguild: Join the Highrise Discord and sign in again so we can set your ballot name from your server profile.
app.field.pitch.label: Your one-line pitch
app.field.pitch.ph: In a sentence — why should holders vote for you?
app.questions.title: In your own words
app.q.track.q: What have you already done to help HCC succeed? Think experiences, things you've vouched for, or ideas you've helped set in motion — and what came of them.
app.q.theme.q: The Council helps decide the theme and aesthetic of upcoming drops. What creative direction would you push for?
app.q.gen2.q: Gen 2 has been promised since 2023 and holders are still waiting. As the Council helps shape it, what would you push for in its quality and direction — and how should holders get a say before it's final?
app.q.value.q: What's the single biggest thing you'd push the Council to prioritize to make owning a Creature genuinely worth it — and why that one?
app.q.roadmap.q: The Council advises on drop cadence and roadmap. How would you balance shipping fresh drops against finishing Gen 1 & Gen 2?
app.q.communication.q: The Council advises on how HCC communicates with holders. What would you do to rebuild trust and keep people genuinely informed — especially with longtime holders who need to feel their loyalty and support still count?
app.q.represent.q: How would you fairly represent every kind of holder — a single-NFT owner, a whale, a renter, and someone brand new?
app.q.seat.q: The Council decides on creative and advises elsewhere, while Pocket Worlds holds the line on the economy, brand and legal. When the two disagree, how hard should the Council push — and how would you keep it from becoming a scapegoat?
app.consent.seat: I understand a Council seat is tied to me and can't be sold or transferred.
app.consent.publish: I agree my answers may be published for holders to read before voting.
app.consent.hold: I'll keep meeting the eligibility bar through the candidacy window.
app.updated: Changes saved — holders will see the updated version.
app.editing.note: You're editing your live application — changes go public as soon as you save.
app.locked.note: Voting has begun, so your application is locked in — holders are seeing it exactly as you saved it.
app.submitted.p: Holders will see your profile when voting opens. You can edit it any time until voting begins.
app.err.required: Complete every field, set a position on every statement, and tick the acknowledgements before submitting.
app.err.consent: Please tick all three acknowledgements to submit.
app.err.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
app.positions.title: Your positions
app.positions.intro: Set where you stand on each statement. These become your public voting-advice profile, and holders are matched to you on them.
app.derive.hint: Uses AI to suggest a starting position from your written answers — you can adjust every one.
app.derived.ok: Drafted — review and adjust each position below.
prop.quality: The Council should favour fewer, higher-quality drops over more frequent ones.
prop.exclusivity: What earlier holders already received should stay exclusive to them — newer holders shouldn't get the same things back through recolours, similar drops, or marketplace re-releases.
prop.gen2bold: Gen 2 should take bold creative risks rather than play it safe with familiar designs.
prop.gen2focus: If Gen 2 keeps slipping, the Council should redirect that effort into steady drops and perks instead.
prop.transparency: The Council should communicate openly and often, even when there's little news to share.
prop.newholders: Right now the Council should focus on value for new and small holders over rewarding long-time or large holders.
prop.smallholders: Every holder should have an equal say, whether they hold 1 asset or 100.
prop.pushback: The Council should push Pocket Worlds privately rather than through public pressure.
prop.mandate: The Council should push to expand its decision-making power over time.
